title: Private Deployments — VPC & On‑Prem Reference Architecture, Packaging, and Day‑2 Operations
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Comprehensive reference covering VPC and on‑prem reference architectures, on‑prem packaging, day‑2 operational best practices, upgrade and rollback procedures, and a customer requirements checklist for Private Deployments.
body:
Overview

This document consolidates best practices and prescriptive guidance for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It is intended for solutions engineers, platform operators, SREs, and customer engineering teams responsible for initial deployment, ongoing (day‑2) operations, and upgrade/rollback lifecycle management.

Scope
- VPC-delivered Private deployments (customer VPC peering/transit & private control plane).
- On‑prem/rack deployments with our packaged installer (air‑gapped and connected variants).
- Packaging and installer formats, required host/system configuration, and recommended secure defaults.
- Day‑2 operations: monitoring, capacity, backups, incident response, log access, and maintenance windows.
- Upgrade and rollback procedures with automated and manual paths.
- Customer requirements library (network, security, compliance) and a sample checklist.

Reference Architectures

1) VPC Reference Architecture (recommended for cloud-first customers)
- Topology: Customer VPC <-> Transit / Peering <-> Redwood Private control plane (hosted) + Data plane in customer VPC.
- Key components:
  - Control plane endpoints (hosted, Redwood-managed) exposed via private endpoint (AWS PrivateLink / Azure Private Endpoint / GCP Private Service Connect).
  - Data plane: Kubernetes cluster (managed or self-managed) in customer VPC hosting serving runtime nodes, autoscaling groups, and ingress/nat gateways as required.
  - Networking: Dedicated subnets for serving, management, and storage. Strict security groups and NACLs.
  - Storage: Customer-managed object store (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) for artifacts and KV backup; optional local NVMe for model cache.

Diagram (textual)
Customer VPC: [Bastion] -- [Private Subnet: k8s worker pool] -- [Model Cache NVMe] -- [Egress NAT / PrivateLink] -- Redwood Control Plane (private endpoint)

Networking & Security Recommendations (VPC)
- Minimum: 3 subnets across 2 AZs (control, serving, storage).
- Security groups:
  - Control plane SG: allow outbound to Redwood control plane endpoints on TLS (443) and NTP (123).
  - Node SG: restrict incoming to LB/ingress and management bastion only.
- Route table: route to NAT for external registries; explicit route to PrivateLink endpoint.
- DNS: Use conditional forwarders or private hosted zones for control plane endpoints.

2) On‑Prem / Air‑Gapped Reference Architecture (recommended for highly regulated customers)
- Topology: Physical racks or private cloud with isolated management network; optional egress via approved proxy for pull updates.
- Key components:
  - Installer package: curated tarball + container registry bundle (OCI tar), pre-signed manifests.
  - Local registry: recommended (Harbor/Artifactory) with signed images and attestation.
  - Model storage: local NFS/NAS with snapshot policies or object store emulator.
  - Orchestration: Kubernetes (Rook/Ceph optional), with CSI drivers for high-performance model storage.

Packaging and Installer

Delivery formats
- Connected installer: Helm charts + small bootstrap container that pulls images from Redwood mirrors.
- Air‑gapped installer: OCI image bundle (tar.gz), installation manifests, and a signed release manifest.
- Configuration: templated kustomize overlays and values.yaml for environment-specific settings.

Installer checklist
- Signed release manifest verified by checksum and public key.
- Image bundle imported into the local registry before installation.
- Values file validated against schema (provided by Redwood) with 'redwood-validate' CLI.

Deployment Prerequisites (minimum supported configuration)

| Component           | Minimum | Recommended | Notes |
|---------------------|---------|-------------|-------|
| Kubernetes version  | 1.22    | 1.24+       | Must support alpha APIs used by CSI/EPHEMERAL volume features; check release notes. |
| GPU per node        | 1x A10  | 2x A100 / H200 | For inference heavy workloads use multi-GPU nodes with MIG or device plugin. |
| Worker nodes (vCPU)| 8       | 16+         | Dependent on throughput and model size. |
| Memory per node     | 32GB    | 128GB+      | Model KV cache and serving memory use can be high for large models. |
| Local NVMe          | optional| recommended  | Model cache; improves cold-start latency. |
| Storage (object)    | required| recommended  | S3/GCS/Azure Blob or on-prem object store. |
| TLS & KMS           | required| required    | TLS certs for mTLS; KMS/HSM for key protection. |

Note: adjust sizes per model (see model onboarding docs).

Day‑2 Operations

Observability and Metrics
- Required metrics: request latency (P50/P95/P99), tokens/sec, error rate, GPU util, memory pressure, KV cache hit rate.
- Dashboards: per-cluster and per-model dashboards in Redwood Console or Grafana.
- Logs: structured request logs, audit logs for control plane actions, and GPU driver logs collected centrally.

Capacity & Autoscaling
- Horizontal autoscaler for replica-level traffic; cluster autoscaler for node-level changes.
- Recommended autoscaling policy:
  - Target GPU utilization: 60-75% for steady-state to allow headroom for bursts.
  - Scale up threshold: 70% utilization sustained for 2 minutes.
  - Scale down cooldown: 10 minutes to avoid oscillation.

Backups & Disaster Recovery
- Backup schedule: nightly snapshot of object store metadata and weekly snapshot of local volumes.
- Recovery RPO/RTO targets: define with customer; default recommendation: RPO 24h / RTO 4h for non-critical deployments.
- Test recovery quarterly.

Maintenance Windows & Patch Management
- Regular maintenance cadence: monthly minor patches, quarterly kernel/GPU driver updates, annual major upgrades.
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic to canary nodes for 24-48 hours before broader rollout.

Runbook — Common Day‑2 Procedures
1) Add capacity (scale cluster)
   - Review current GPU util and queue depth.
   - Update MachinePool/NodeGroup spec and trigger autoscaler.
   - Validate cluster healthy, pods scheduled and model cache warming.
2) Replace faulty GPU node
   - Cordone node: kubectl cordon <node>.
   - Evict pods gracefully: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data.
   - Replace hardware and rejoin to cluster.
3) Certificate rotation
   - Generate cert in KMS or on-prem CA.
   - Update secret in namespace redwood-system and restart control-plane pods in a rolling fashion.

Upgrade and Rollback Procedures

Guiding principles
- Always run a preflight validation (checksums, schema validation, available disk, registry health).
- Use canary-first rollouts and automated health checks.
- Keep a tested rollback procedure with clear artifact pins (image digests, config hashes).

Automated Upgrade (preferred for connected deployments)
1) Prepare release: obtain signed release manifest and release notes.
2) Run preflight: redwood-validate --manifest release-manifest.yaml.
3) Create canary: apply kustomize overlay for canary (replica fraction 5%).
4) Monitor health for 1-2 hours (P95 latency, error rate, GPU OOMs).
5) Gradually increase fraction to 25% -> 50% -> 100% with health gates at each step.
6) If failure observed, trigger rollback to prior image digests and config hash.

Manual Upgrade (on‑prem / air‑gapped)
1) Import OCI bundle to local registry.
2) Update values.yaml with pinned image digests.
3) Apply manifest to canary overlay.
4) Validate and proceed as automated path.

Rollback procedure (if automated rollback fails)
- Step 1: Pause traffic with ingress annotation to drain new pods.
- Step 2: Re-deploy previous pinned manifests (image digests + config).
- Step 3: If state migration occurred and cannot be reversed, perform restore from snapshot (follow DR runbook).
- Step 4: Open a cross-functional incident, capture timelines and logs, and create a postmortem.

Customer Requirements Library (sample items)

| Category       | Customer ask / requirement | Redwood default / guidance | Implementation notes |
|----------------|----------------------------|----------------------------|----------------------|
| Network        | Private connectivity only  | PrivateLink / Private Endpoint recommended | Provide endpoint IPs and DNS entries; test latency < 20ms to control plane. |
| Data residency | Data must remain in region X | Deploy data plane in region X and leverage local object store | Confirm backups do not replicate outside region. |
| Encryption     | Customer keys for secrets  | Integrate with customer KMS/HSM via KMIP / Cloud KMS | Use envelope encryption for object store. |
| Compliance     | FedRAMP / ISO controls     | Provide evidence package and scoped controls | Engage security/compliance for assessment. |

Customer checklist (pre-deployment)
- [ ] VPC subnet allocations and route tables configured.
- [ ] Private endpoint / firewall rules opened to Redwood control plane endpoints.
- [ ] Local registry available and accessible.
- [ ] TLS certs and KMS access validated.
- [ ] GPU drivers and device plugin installed and tested.
- [ ] Snapshot/backup configuration in place.

Operational Ownership and Contacts
- Owner (Redwood): Private Deployments team (eng-private-deployments). Primary: Aisha Patel (solutions lead).
- Escalation path: oncall -> eng-sre -> platform -> security if data exposure suspected.
- Support artifacts to include with escalations: cluster diagnostics bundle (redwood-diagnose.tar.gz), logs (last 48h), and reproducible request sample.

Appendix A — Example CLI snippets
- Validate manifest (connected):
  redwood-validate --manifest release-manifest.yaml --kube-context prod-customer-1
- Import OCI bundle (air-gapped):
  skopeo copy oci-archive:bundle.tar oci://localhost:5000/redwood/bundle:2027-03-10
- Create canary overlay:
  kustomize build overlays/canary | kubectl apply -f -

Appendix B — Example values.yaml excerpt
  redwood:
    replicas: 4
    modelCache:
      localNVMe: true
      cacheSizeGiB: 512
    metrics:
      enabled: true
    auth:
      tls: true
      mtls: true
